rationales: A system does not necessarily work independently; it may interact with other systems or its environment.
A system’s primary function is to organize its components and activities to achieve a common goal.
Creating new systems is not the primary function of a system.
Providing entertainment may be the purpose of some systems, but it is not the primary function of systems in general.
A system can be large or small, so size is not a fundamental concept that defines it.
An objective is fundamental because it describes what the system is intended to achieve.
A system’s age does not define its fundamental nature.
A system’s price is not a fundamental concept of systems.
The human body is a complex system with many interacting parts.
A computer network is generally more complex than a simple system.
A thermostat regulating temperature is a simple system that senses temperature and controls heating or cooling.
The Internet is a large and highly complex system.
A dynamic environment changes over time, whether or not the system produces an output.
A static environment remains unchanged unless an output from the system affects it.
A deterministic system produces predictable results from given inputs; this does not describe an unchanged environment.
A non-deterministic system may produce unpredictable results; this does not describe an unchanged environment.
Users, hardware, and software can be parts of some systems but do not describe the basic components of a system in general.
Objectives, components, environment, and communication describe the basic components of a system.
Inputs, outputs, and processes describe a common way of representing system operations, but not the full set of basic components asked for here.
Sensors, actuators, and controllers are components of some control systems, not systems in general.
Hardware design is only one possible application of systems theory, not its overall focus.
Systems theory seeks to understand how systems interact and develop over time.
Software applications are a specific topic and are not the general focus of systems theory.
Network security is a specialized field rather than the general subject of systems theory.
The processor performs calculations and executes instructions; the OS manages and coordinates computer operations.
Main memory temporarily stores data and instructions for the CPU, rather than serving as the OS.
The OS manages computer operations and responds to input by directing appropriate actions.
Long-term storage devices provide persistent storage, rather than serving as the OS.
Separate memories for data and instructions are characteristic of Harvard architecture, not the standard Von Neumann architecture.
Parallel instruction execution is not the defining characteristic of Von Neumann architecture.
Von Neumann architecture uses a single memory store for both program instructions and data.
Using multiple CPUs is not the defining characteristic of Von Neumann architecture.
Separate memory spaces are not a design feature of the Von Neumann architecture.
Programs stored in memory can generally be modified, so this is not its key disadvantage.
Sharing a single memory and communication path for instructions and data can create a bottleneck.
Von Neumann architecture is flexible in executing instructions; its key disadvantage is the shared-memory bottleneck.
The Control Unit directs and coordinates operations but does not itself transport data among components.
The System Bus transports data among a computer’s components.
Memory stores data and instructions rather than transporting them among components.
The processor executes instructions and processes data, while the bus carries data between components.
